correctness.rationale: Exchangeability gives the reciprocal path-size marginal. For two comparable distinct vertices, their record events are tests of two independent insertion ranks in the uniform relative ordering of the longer path (the insertion-rank vector is in bijection with the full permutation). For incomparable vertices transform marks to independent uniform survival values. On t<s the integrand is t^(k+a-1)s^(b-1) and integrates to 1/[(k+a)(k+a+b)]; the other half gives the analogous k+b term. Subtracting the marginal product gives the positive covariance claimed. The unique zero-covariance candidate at the preceding depth is then the parent; the root is identified by marginal one. For independent repeated vectors, the n+binom(n,2) bounded scalar averages obey the simultaneous Hoeffding bound with error eta=1/(24n^3); no within-vector independence is needed. The smallest spacing of reciprocal depth means is 1/[n(n-1)] and covariance error is at most 3 eta. The three covariance denominator factors are at most n (the largest is the union size k+a+b), so the record's weaker lower bound 1/[n^2(2n-1)] also holds. The stated depth rounding, 1/(4n^3) threshold, and sufficient replication count therefore work, including with the root constant and with no incomparable pair. The supplied finite checker and its reported output were inspected, not executed; the uniform bound is proved analytically.
residual_risks: Repeated measurements must be complete vectors with stable vertex identities and independent redraws of iid atomless marks.
The sample bound is sufficient, not claimed optimal; possible ambiguity of a candidate outside the good event can be handled as a failure of reconstruction.

evidence: The accessible Janson abstract concerns the forward equality in distribution between random cuts and records. Burghart's abstract gives completeness for certain polynomial invariants of rooted trees/forests up to isomorphism. The distinct Resultary result gives covariance-sign recovery for a different noisy event-tree model, after contracting maximal unary runs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Completeness of different polynomial invariants does not identify a labeled tree from these observed first/pairwise moments. The related event-tree theorem is not stronger for the claimed data: it has different covariances and expressly works on a unary-contracted object. Janson full-text coverage remains unverified.

evidence: Minimum and maximum path records are equivalent under reversal of the mark order; no parametric mark distribution is required. The closest distinct compared record concerns sampled-vertex path tracing with noisy binary edge observations, not new records of independent marks at all vertices.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the sampled-vertex observation one root path is traced per draw, and exclusive events compete for that draw. Path records arise simultaneously across branches from independent marks, with positive incomparable covariances and zero comparable covariances. A reversal of mark order or sign convention does not turn one model into the other.

value.rationale: This turns a standard forward process into a concrete inverse result with severe data compression: one synchronized bit per label suffices as a repeated observation, and only first and pairwise means are needed. The explicit nonvanishing separation provides a noise-to-exact-recovery guarantee for every rooted labeled tree, not just for a random-tree ensemble or a restricted degree class.
residual_risks: No reconstruction from aggregate counts, unlabeled vectors, or a single experiment; no sharp sample rate is established.
